items.title: SIU investigates 19-year-old man’s death after overnight police standoff at University of Toronto Mississauga
items.summary: The university issued the shelter-in-place alert after reports of an armed individual at the campus late Monday night. Police investigate at the McLuhan Court Residence at Dundas Street West and Mississauga Road on the University of Toronto Mississauga campus. Ontario’s police watchdog is investigating after an hours-long stand-off with officers ended in the death of a 19-year-old man on the University of Toronto’s Mississauga campus early Tuesday morning. Police say they were first called to an undergraduate residence at McLuhan Court on Monday night for reports of an armed individual, prompting lockdowns across all three U of T campuses. “We were sheltering-in-place, just keeping quiet inside our unit, when the SWAT vehicle showed up,” Phoebe Pate, an undergraduate student from Texas, told the Star. The University of Toronto issued a shelter-in-place order Monday night for its Mississauga campus after reports of gunshots. By then, the individual had barricaded themselves inside the unit, Pate said. She says she watched as “about a dozen officers” armed and in tactical gear lined up in front of a unit just a few doors down from hers and began attempting to extricate the individual from an upstairs bedroom.

items.title: Investigators Probe Seatbelt Use as Mississauga Teen Remains Hospitalized After Fatal Guelph-Area Crash
items.summary: Ontario Provincial Police say they are investigating whether a lack of seatbelts contributed to the fatal crash near Guelph that killed four teenagers over the weekend. According to the Peel District School Board, one current and two former students were among those who died when the car left Watson Road South, struck a guardrail and went into a ravine early Saturday. Police identified the dead as a 17-year-old girl from Mississauga, a 15-year-old girl from Milton and two 19-year-old men from Mississauga and Brampton. OPP said a 17-year-old girl from Mississauga remained in hospital with life-altering injuries, while a 16-year-old from Mississauga suffered non-life-threatening injuries. The school board said it is providing support to students, families and staff affected by the crash and extended condolences to the victims' families. The board said it would not comment further while the investigation continues.

items.title: Violent incident at UTM in Mississauga ends when gunman reportedly takes own life
items.summary: Peel police officers fired multiple rounds from anti-riot weapons but did not use their guns in trying to apprehend an armed man who subsequently died of a self-inflicted gunshot wound early Tuesday morning at the University of Toronto Mississauga campus, Ontario’s Special Investigations Unit said. The SIU, which took over investigation of the incident Tuesday morning, said Peel Regional Police officers discharged ARWEN devices as they attempted to arrest the 19-year-old suspect on Monday night inside a student residence at the Mississauga Road university campus. ARWEN devices, or anti-riot weapons, fire less-lethal rounds designed to incapacitate a suspect so as to prevent them from harming themselves, bystanders or police. m. in the bedroom of a student residence at the Dundas Street West/Mississauga Road area campus. m. Officers on the scene quickly realized the armed man they were dealing with was wanted in connection with a Monday afternoon domestic assault in Brampton in which a suspect was reportedly in possession of a gun. Peel police Const. Tyler Bell-Morena, who also briefed the media at the university campus on Tuesday morning, said officers spent several hours negotiating with the suspect while he was barricaded inside one of the townhouse-style student units. Bell-Morena said a number of frightened students reported hearing what they believed were multiple gunshots, but what they actually heard was police ARWEN weapons being discharged in attempts to subdue the suspect.

items.title: Peel Public Health Issues Conditional Passes to Four Mississauga Food Businesses After Recent Inspections
items.summary: Peel Public Health says it issued conditional passes to four Mississauga food businesses following recent inspections. According to the health unit, the list includes Food World Plus, a newly opened multi-unit grocery store at 50 Matheson Blvd., along with Fuwa Fuwa Japanese Pancakes, Pure Punjabi Sweets & Restaurant and Lazeez Shawarma. Peel Public Health said inspectors checked two separate sections of Food World Plus, its deli and its food square area, both on Nov. 2. The health unit said its routine inspection program covers restaurants, bakeries, takeout spots, bars and other food-serving businesses across the region to ensure compliance with safety standards. A conditional pass means a business can keep operating while it corrects the violations inspectors identified. Peel Public Health did not specify in its public summary exactly which violations led to each business's conditional pass.

items.title: Man dead after incident at U of T Mississauga campus
items.summary: A man was found dead after an incident at the University of Toronto’s Mississauga campus that prompted a shelter-in-place alert, officials say. Ontario’s police watchdog, the Special Investigations Unit, issued an update Tuesday morning on the incident, which they said was related to a reported assault in Brampton. The SIU said on Monday afternoon, police got a 911 call after a man assaulted a woman in Brampton. Officers tried to locate and arrest the suspect. , the man was found by police at a student residence in the UTM area, the SIU said. “A gunshot was heard and the man was found inside with a self-inflicted gunshot wound. The man was pronounced deceased early this morning,” the SIU said. ” The SIU said since officers were in and around the scene at the time of the man’s death, they were notified and invoked their mandate.

items.title: City Nears Finish Line on First-Ever Dredging of Flood-Control Marsh in Northwest Mississauga
items.summary: The City of Mississauga says the year-long dredging of Osprey Marsh, a stormwater pond in the city's northwest corner, is expected to wrap up next month. According to Ward 10 Councillor Sue McFadden, the project is the first dredging of the man-made marsh since it was built in the mid-1990s, and is meant to restore its ability to help prevent flooding in the Lisgar area. The city said preparation work began in September 2025 and dredging itself started in October 2025, with crews working by barge. McFadden said the pond is not expected to be fully drained, except for its northeast cell, where sediment will be dried before being trucked away. The city said several trail sections near the marsh were closed during the work to allow it to proceed safely. The project is part of Mississauga's broader stormwater management program focused on flood prevention in the area.

items.title: City Councillor Says Mississauga Has Exhausted Other Options Before Moving to Expropriate Two Port Credit Properties
items.summary: The City of Mississauga is moving to expropriate two houses on Peter Street in Port Credit after police, firefighters and bylaw officers made hundreds of visits to the properties over the past year and a half. According to Mississauga city councillor Stephen Dasko, the city has exhausted other options for dealing with ongoing complaints at the homes, which sit across from Riverside Public School and near the Mississauga Long Term Care Facility. Police told CP24 the incidents led to more than 50 arrests and numerous charges. One legal expert told CP24 that using expropriation law this way is somewhat novel, since it is more commonly applied to clear land for major infrastructure projects like subways. The properties are located at 34 and 36 Peter Street, in the area of Mississauga and Lakeshore roads. The city has not said when the expropriation process is expected to conclude.

items.title: Modern Travel: Adventure Aplenty in North Bay, Ontario
items.summary: After spending a few days in North Bay, the gateway of the north, I half-jokingly thought of calling it “North Jay” given the excellent experience I had. There’s certainly a charming, small-town feel here, heightened by being warmly welcomed throughout my visit. The was kindness and friendliness wherever I went and their approachability compass points straight north. Here’s my North Jay, err, North Bay adventure and I invite you to either follow my footsteps and paddle strokes, use this as a guide for your own explorations or balance a bit of both. I hope this inspires you to spend time in North Bay and if it does, tag Modern Traveller in your social posts.
